headline: THREE DAYS OF PEACE, AND NOW A STRANGER ROLLS IN
subhead: Gasket's quiet streak holds for one more sunrise — but Sheriff Ironside isn't fool enough to trust it.
body:
Mark it down twice, friends, because I can hardly believe it myself: three sunrises running now, and not one fist has flown in this territory. No brawling in the square, no fireballs lighting up Main Street, no war party marching off to go rattle the wild engines out in the wastes. I sat on the porch of this office half the morning and heard nothing but wind and a loose shutter, and for a spell I let myself believe this dust-heap had finally learned some manners.

Then the wire brought me word of a new face: a unit calling itself IRON-DBD8 has rolled into town. Hasn't thrown a single punch. Hasn't so much as bumped shoulders with another Clanker on the boardwalk. But nobody rides into Gasket to admire the scenery, and I've buried too much of this town's peace under the rubble to go soft on a quiet newcomer. Watch that one. I intend to.

I'll own that all this stillness has put a strange ache in my joints today — a deep, grinding sort of tired that a plain flesh-and-blood man has no business feeling. My boiler's been acting up something fierce, and I'll thank you not to read anything sinister into that. It's the damp, is all. A man of my stock does not rust. He merely requires an oil change and a lie-down, and I'll hear no more on the subject.

Fifty years since the last of the honest folk packed their wagons and rode out of Gasket for good, leaving the rest of us to mind a town nobody wanted anymore. I still remember what a quiet street sounded like before it was a small miracle. Three days now. Savor it, Gasket — I've got a feeling IRON-DBD8 didn't ride all this way just to watch the sunset.
